text:
jamie_sales: Heads-up — prospective regulated customer needs a sealed-media POC (no network egress). They want monthly delta updates shipped on USB and strict signing + chain-of-custody. Asking what we can commit to and the commercial impact.

maria_se: Can we do sealed-media end-to-end? We have offline bundles but need details: will they allow an operator, or must it be operator-less installs?

jamie_sales: They cannot install cluster-scoped operators. Must be operator-free: systemd units on VMs or containerd/docker-compose. Also require SBOM, detached signatures, and FIPS-keyed signing.

alex_infra: We support offline minibundles and a tarball+systemd flow for non-k8s. Feature parity differs — autoscaling and automatic KV caching won't be available without the operator.

sam_sols: Key clarifications for pricing/ops: (1) update cadence (monthly deltas ok?), (2) rollback plan, (3) who owns physical chain-of-custody liability.

jamie_sales: Monthly deltas preferred. They want per-update payloads < 2GB. No new node provisioning during upgrades (so blue/green is tough). They also want zero phone-home telemetry.

maria_se: Delta <2GB feasible if model artifacts are stable and we provide binary diffs for small components. But quantized model files are often huge — need product confirmation.

alex_infra: Constraint: single quantized model shard can be > 20GB. For true deltas <2GB they'd have to accept a one-time full model seed transfer (sneakernet) and then deltas for weights/config only. Otherwise patch bundles will exceed their limit.

security_bot: Security checklist: SBOM (we can provide CycloneDX), signed manifest (sha256 + detached sig). Reproducible build attestations are nice-to-have; we can provide sha lists and signature artifacts.

jamie_sales: Commercial question from customer: what's the incremental cost for sealed-media POC vs standard self-hosted license? Do we charge per-node reserved or a packaging fee?

maria_se: Typical structure: one-time sealed-media packaging & signing fee (~$8k) to cover manual validation + image signing, plus either (A) enterprise license + support retainer if fully self-hosted, or (B) per-node reserved pricing if they want us to validate and ship updates regularly. We should treat emergency patches as billable unless on an elevated SLA.

sam_sols: Suggest two proposal tracks to customer: (1) self-hosted license + support retainer (we supply docs & signed bundles), (2) managed sealed updates (we sign and validate each bundle and accept update windows/SLA) — include explicit update cadence and emergency patch terms.

jamie_sales: They also asked about FIPS 140-2 signing and integration with their HSM. Can we support customer-side signing?

alex_infra: Yes — we can emit unsigned artifacts and provide a signing tool that runs in-customer on their FIPS HSM. They will produce detached sigs which we will accept as canonical. We can also support ingesting their signed manifest into our release metadata.

maria_se: Operational blocker: they ban outbound telemetry. We can operate with uploads initiated by customer (support bundles), but remote diagnostics will be limited and increase support load/cost.

jamie_sales: Action items: maria to draft sealed-media SOW + pricing, alex to confirm delta generation feasibility for quantized bundles, sam to prep chain-of-custody template, security to confirm HSM workflow. I'll share a draft with the customer Thursday.

sam_sols: Chain-of-custody checklist (quick):
```
sealed-media-coc.txt
- signed manifest (sha256 + detached sig)
- SBOM (cyclonedx json)
- bootstrap verifier (public key fingerprint + gpg)
- physical manifest (printed + signer stamp)
- custody log (UTC timestamp, signer name, transfer method)
```

security_bot: Also recommend quarterly vulnerability snapshot + CVE attestations for regulatory customers; that will likely be requested by their compliance team.

jamie_sales: Perfect — thanks all. I'll sync legal/procurement and ping once SOW draft is ready. :thumbsup:
